who: GPT-6 Astra Pro, distributed transport review lane
what: Ordinary imports passed only a pack digest to the HTTP fetch and could buffer up to the 4 GiB blob ceiling before discovering that a manifest committed a much smaller length. Read-ahead already enforced the committed length. Ordinary cache requests also used separate blocking socket timeouts, so continuing partial progress could repeatedly restart the allowance.
cost: A malformed response could consume multi-GiB memory for a small committed pack; slow partial transfers could outlive the configured request timeout.
cause: The importer erased the size commitment at its fetch callback, and ordinary requests used a separate IO path from the bounded read-ahead operations.
whys: The pack decoder checked length only after the HTTP body was buffered.
The ordinary fetch callback received a digest without its committed length.
Only the read-ahead path called the existing bounded pack reader.
The API made the unbounded form shorter even when the caller held a complete PackRef.
class: resource bounds are discarded between a commitment and the IO that consumes its bytes
prevention: The importer fetch callback requires PackRef, committed_pack passes its size to the bounded HTTP reader, native manifest lengths obey the blob ceiling, and ordinary request phases share one absolute deadline.
fix: Added causal ordinary-import socket coverage, exact manifest boundary coverage and expired-budget controls; retained the existing fragmented-response and allocation oracles.
state: Implemented; exact-tree native validation is pending with the main lane.
